The present application under Section 430 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (hereinafter 'BNSS') (corresponding to Section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure) has been filed by the appellant/applicant seeking suspension of sentence.

2. The brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present application are that FIR No. 501/2019 was registered at the instance of the mother of the victim against the applicant under Sections 376 and 376AB of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter "IPC") and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter "POCSO Act").

4. sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that the applicant has undergone more than five years of the awarded sentence.

It is further submitted that the likelihood of the appeal being heard in the near future is bleak and that the appeal raises arguable grounds which would require detailed examination when the appeal is finally heard.

6. Per contra, learned APP appearing for the State strongly opposes the application and submits that, considering the severity of the offence, namely aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon a minor who is mentally disabled, the applicant does not deserve the exercise of discretion in his favour.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents on record, including the Nominal roll dated 23.09.2025, which reflects that the applicant has undergone only 5 years and 11 months out of the awarded sentence of 20 years.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

This Court is of the view that, at this stage, the gravity of the offence and the unexpired portion of the sentence are vital considerations.
The offence in question, namely aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon a minor, is undoubtedly grave, particularly in view of its serious ramifications on the victim.
Further, the applicant is yet to undergo a substantial portion of the sentence awarded.
Weighing these considerations, this Court is of the opinion that it would be premature to suspend the sentence of the applicant at this stage.
9. Accordingly, the present application stands dismissed.

10. It is clarified that nothing stated herein shall be construed as an expression on the merits of the case, and all rights and contentions of the parties are kept open to be urged at the time of final hearing.
AJAY DIGPAUL, J DECEMBER 23, 2025 gs/yr
